A.notes: A has a clear SaaS idea built around isolating one anomalous log line, and the hero/demo visuals explain the product fast. The typography is strong and the desktop composition is clean, but the overall language feels familiar rather than distinctive. Motion appears minimal in the scroll strip, and the mobile product section looks under-resolved with a large blank area where the working demo should carry more of the page.

B.notes: B has the stronger single idea: an on-call editorial/workbench aesthetic where routine lines pass and the one that matters is isolated. The serif/mono system gives it a distinctive voice without fighting the developer-tool brief, and the scroll strip shows a more narrative motion sequence tied to the product story. Craft is high across desktop and mobile, though the product-at-work section seems to rely on scroll state more heavily, which makes some static captures look sparse before the sequence completes.

raw.why: B carries a more original and cohesive concept through type, structure, and motion while still clearly demonstrating the product.
